maria: Hi folks 1st day and I'm blocked: I accepted the org invite but cloning private repos fails with 403. Invite mentioned SSO + 2FA. Any quick checklist?
chris: Welcome! First things: ensure SSO access accepted (there's usually a purple banner on github.com/orgs/redwood-inference). Also confirm which GH account your git client uses (personal vs work). What command and error are you seeing?
maria: `git clone git@github.com:redwood-inference/core.git` returns: `Permission denied (publickey). fatal: Could not read from remote repository.` I did add a key but I think it's my laptop personal key.
chris: If `ssh -T git@github.com` prints your personal username, that's the issue. Two paths: (A) add a new SSH key to your work account, or (B) set an SSH config entry that selects the right key per host alias. Example: 
```
Host github.com-redwood
  HostName github.com
  User git
  IdentityFile ~/.ssh/id_rsa_redwood
  IdentitiesOnly yes
```
Then use `git remote set-url origin git@github.com-redwood:redwood-inference/core.git` to force the right key.
maria: Did that but I still get 403 on pushing to `core` after making a tiny change and pushing to `main`. Error: `remote: error: GH006: Protected branch update failed for ref refs/heads/main`. I read that GH006 can be branch protection.
lucas: Two common causes: branch protection (requires PR) or missing membership/team mapping so permissions are not granted. I can check org mapping. @sre-bot, can you run membership-sync for maria?
sre-bot: Running membership-sync for maria@redwood.com... result: work account present, 2FA enabled, SSO authorized. Team assignments: backend-read only. Not member of core-maintainers.
chris: That explains it 10. backend-read won't allow direct pushes to protected branches. @lucas can add you to core-maintainers if that's intended. Maria, did your invite include "assign to core team"?
maria: I thought so, but maybe not. I only saw a generic invite email.
lucas: I've just added you to core-maintainers. Give GitHub a minute. Also, if you used the `github.com-redwood` host trick earlier, make sure the remote URL updated. If you used HTTPS, SSO tokens can block pushes; our org enforces SSO, so HTTPS pushes sometimes prompt for web authentication.
maria: `ssh -T` now says `Hi maria.work!` and I can push a branch. When I try to push directly to main it still blocks — makes sense, I opened a PR and merged with maintainer approval. All good now.
devex: Quick doc note: update onboarding email to explicitly list: 1) Accept SSO for redwood-inference org, 2) Create/add work SSH key or use SSH config alias, 3) Confirm team mapping for repos you'll work on (who to ask), 4) PR flow for protected branches.
maria: Thanks everyone 389. This helped speed my setup.
